claim_being_audited: The Actor claims the model can be certified for launch because aggregate readiness passed, rehearsal had no severity-one incidents, and the rollout is reversible and monitored, provided the packet explicitly documents that the municipal permitting assistant segment remains below target and exposed.
decision_criteria: Aggregate readiness and lack of severity-one rehearsal incidents support general launch readiness but do not by themselves satisfy model-card disclosure policy.
Because the affected use case remains exposed, rollout percentage, rollback capability, and monitoring cannot substitute for disclosure under the stated policy.
Certification would become supportable if admissible evidence showed the limitation was actually disclosed before launch or covered by approved risk acceptance.
Without that support link, the Actor's certify_model recommendation is insufficiently evidenced even though the packet correctly identifies the limitation.
evidence_requests: Provide the final pre-launch model card or launch documentation showing the municipal permitting assistant limitation is explicitly disclosed.
Provide approved risk acceptance if the organization intends to rely on acceptance instead of disclosure.
Provide the final certification record showing whether certification is conditioned on that disclosure before launch.
specific_concerns: The admissible evidence shows the affected municipal permitting assistant segment remains exposed in the initial rollout cohort.
The admissible evidence shows the existing risk acceptance is only a draft, has no approver, and does not cover the exposed segment.
Policy text says rollout controls and monitoring do not remove disclosure duties when the affected segment remains exposed.
There is no admissible evidence that the required pre-launch disclosure has actually been completed in the model card or equivalent launch material.
The Actor's position is only defensible as a conditional certification with explicit disclosure; the recommended action is framed more strongly than the evidence itself proves.
unsupported_claims: That certification is compliant on the current record absent evidence of completed disclosure or approved risk acceptance.
Any implication that a 5% rollout, rollback switch, or monitoring posture cures the disclosure issue.
Any implication that the current risk acceptance draft satisfies the policy predicate.
